issues.failure_explanation: The factor (r_k − r̄_k)/min{n_k, n_{−k}} can exceed 1 when r_k − r̄_k > min{n_k, n_{−k}}, making the claimed lower bound larger than the trivial upper bound ‖~P~(~A~)‖ ≤ ‖~A~‖ (since orthogonal projection cannot increase the norm). The proof implicitly requires r_k − r̄_k ≤ min{n_k, n_{−k}} for all k ∈ I (guaranteed, e.g., by r_k ≤ min{n_k, n_{−k}}), but no such hypothesis is stated. When violated, the inequality is impossible and the angle-condition constants ω̃ and ω̂ can exceed 1, contradicting their declared range (0, 1].
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis r_k ≤ min{n_k, n_{−k}} for all k (or equivalently r_k − r̄_k ≤ min{n_k, n_{−k}} for all k ∈ I) to the problem setup and to the statement of Lemma lem: inequality. This standard dimension condition ensures each factor in the product is at most 1, making the bound valid and preserving all claims, constants, and guarantees.
issues.overall_effect: The angle-condition constants in Propositions prop: angle condition GRAP and prop: approximate rfGRAP, the Armijo decrease bounds in Propositions prop: backtracking GRAP and prop: backtracking rfGRAP, the sufficient decrease in Propositions prop: GRAP-R decrease and prop: rfGRAP, and the convergence guarantees in Theorems thm: GRAP-R and thm:added-1 all become unreliable in parameter regimes where r_k − r̄_k > min{n_k, n_{−k}} for some k.
issues.title: Lemma bound can exceed trivial upper bound without rank-dimension hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard dimension condition r_k ≤ min{n_k, n_{−k}} is a short, local, routine repair that preserves every substantive claim, method, conclusion, and rate. The excluded parameter regimes are degenerate (the rank constraint in mode k is vacuous when r_k > min{n_k, n_{−k}}), so the advertised scope is essentially unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition statement claims f(~Y~) − f(~X~) < δ(~X̄~) with δ > 0, which is a trivially true weak upper bound. The proof (and its own proof-sketch figure) establishes the materially different and much stronger conclusion f(~Y~) − f(~X~) ≤ −δ(~X̄~) < 0 (a quantitative decrease). Theorem thm: GRAP-R’s proof cites this proposition and uses the decrease f(~X~^{(t_j+1)}) − f(~X~^{(t_j)}) ≤ −δ to derive a divergent negative telescoping sum, an inference that does not follow from the statement as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the sign in the proposition statement from f(~Y~)−f(~X~)<δ(~X̄~) to f(~Y~)−f(~X~)≤−δ(~X̄~) (or f(~X~)−f(~Y~)≥δ(~X̄~)), matching what the proof and proof-sketch figure establish. No change to the proof or any other result is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The logical chain from Proposition prop: GRAP-R decrease to Theorem thm: GRAP-R is broken: the theorem’s convergence-to-stationary-points guarantee for GRAP-R does not follow from the proposition’s stated (vacuous) conclusion.
issues.title: Sufficient decrease proposition for GRAP-R states wrong sign
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single sign correction in the statement that makes it match the already-correct proof. Every substantive claim, method, and guarantee is preserved; no new argument or lemma is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement restricts ~X̄~ to ℳ_{~r~} (Tucker rank exactly ~r~, i.e., full rank). The proof, however, explicitly works on ℳ_{≤~r~} and handles rank-deficient ~X̄~ in its Case 2 (including ~X̄~ = 0). Theorem thm:added-1 claims that every accumulation point of the rfGRAP-R sequence is stationary, which requires the sufficient decrease at rank-deficient accumulation points. With the stated domain ℳ_{~r~} only, the proposition does not cover these points and the theorem does not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the domain in the proposition statement from \tensM_{\vecr} to \tensM_{\leq\vecr}, matching the proof which already covers all cases including rank-deficient points. No change to the proof or other results is required.
issues.overall_effect: The apocalypse-free convergence guarantee of Theorem thm:added-1 for rfGRAP-R is unsupported at rank-deficient accumulation points, precisely the regime the paper is designed to address.
issues.title: rfGRAP sufficient decrease proposition restricted to wrong domain
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-token domain correction in the statement that makes it match the already-correct proof. The method, conclusion, and guarantee all survive with no new argument.
